src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: createTask/listTasks only parse request fields and call this.service.createTask / listProjectTasks. No business rules are evaluated in the controller.
src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: requiredText/optionalText/routeParam/body only check the shape and type of incoming input at the HTTP boundary.

src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: errorHandler maps InvalidInputError to 400, TaskAlreadyDoneError to 409, ResourceNotFoundError to 404 and anything else to 500. This is HTTP error translation, which belongs in infrastructure.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file sits in the infrastructure layer and acts as an HTTP adapter. Everything it does is transport work: it registers Express routes, extracts and type-checks request bodies, query strings and route params, calls application service methods, and maps errors to HTTP status codes. The checks in requiredText, optionalText, routeParam and body only confirm that inputs have the right shape and type at the transport boundary. They do not encode domain rules. Business decisions stay behind TaskService, such as whether a task can be marked done (TaskAlreadyDoneError) and whether a resource exists. The file contains no persistence logic and no domain logic. Matching on error.name === "ResourceNotFoundError" is fragile, but it is still transport-level error mapping, so it is not a layer violation.
